title: Demand to introduce more National-Level Schemes for the comprehensive development of tribal community in Odisha

[ 04 February, 2025 ] 21
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: The following hon. Members associated themselves with
the matter raised by hon. Member, Shri R. Girirajan: Shri Niranjan Bishi (Odisha),
Dr. Sasmit Patra (Odisha), Dr. John Brittas (Kerala), Dr. Kanimozhi NVN Somu
(Tamil Nadu), Shrimati Jebi Mather Hisham (Kerala), Shri M. Shanmugam (Tamil

Shri Niranjan Bishi--Demand to introduce more National-Level Schemes for
the comprehensive development of tribal community in Odisha.
Demand to introduce more National-Level Schemes for the comprehensive
development of tribal community in Odisha
SHRI NIRANJAN BISHI (Odisha): Thank you, hon. Deputy Chairman, Sir, for giving
me an opportunity to speak on an important matter for the development of tribal
community in Odisha. The Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAAGY),
initiated by the Central Government, aims to uplift tribal villages by enhancing their
infrastructure and providing essential services. The evident challenge of weak service
delivery in tribal-inhabited areas necessitates prompt attention. While the PMAAGY
Scheme contributes to the distribution of basic services in tribal villages, concerns
arise over the significant decrease of 63 per cent in fund allocation to Odisha from the
Financial Year 2022-23 to 2023-24. Moreover, Odisha’s fund allocation is
comparatively lower than other States.
The Odisha Government led by hon. Ex-Chief Minister Shri Naveen Patnaikji
had implemented various schemes, such as the Odisha Particularly Vulnerable Tribal
Group Empowerment and Livelihood Improvement Programme (OPELIP), the
Special Development Council (SDC) & Tribal Sub-Plan to uplift the tribal
community. However, there remains a pressing need for increased Central
intervention and assistance in this endeavour.
To address this issue, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, could
consider allocating more funds to Odisha under The Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram
Yojana Scheme, the Special Development Council & Tribal Sub-Plan. Additionally,
launching special programmes and schemes, in collaboration with NGOs, civil society
organizations, and local tribal leaders, can enhance the effective implementation and
monitoring of development programmes and fostering community participation.

22 [ RAJYA SABHA ]
Therefore, through you, Sir, I respectfully urge upon the Government to swiftly
undertake these measures facilitating the comprehensive development of the tribal
community of Odisha and ensuring equitable progress in-line with national objectives.
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: The following hon. Members associated themselves with
the matter raised by Shri Niranjan Bishi: Dr. Fauzia Khan (Maharashtra), Shri P. P.
Suneer (Kerala), Shri R. Girirajan (Tamil Nadu), Shri Subhasish Khuntia (Odisha),
Shrimati Sulata Deo (Odisha), Shri Muzibulla Khan (Odisha), Shri A. A. Rahim
(Kerala), Dr. John Brittas (Kerala), Dr. Sasmit Patra (Odisha), Shri Prakash Chik
Baraik (West Bengal), Shri Saket Gokhale (West Bengal), Shrimati Mahua Maji
(Jharkhand) and Shri M. Mohamed Abdulla (Tamil Nadu).
Shri Ritabrata Banerjee; demand for changing the name of West Bengal to
Bangla.
Demand for changing the name of West Bengal to Bangla
SHRI RITABRATA BANERJEE (West Bengal): Sir, it is a long-pending demand of the
th
State of West Bengal to change the name of the State to Bangla. On July 26 , 2018,
the State Assembly, under the leadership of Mamata Banerjee unanimously passed a
Resolution to change the name of our State from West Bengal to Bangla. All sorts of
clarifications were given in this regard.…(Interruptions)…
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Please. …(Interruptions)… आप बठै जाएं। आपकी बात िरकाडर्
पर नहीं जाएगी। Please take your seat. …(Interruptions)…
SHRI RITABRATA BANERJEE: Hon. Chief Minister of Bengal, Shrimati Mamata
Banerjee, has time and again requested to fast-track the approval. Mamata Banerjee,
“
in her letter to the hon. Prime Minister has categorically stated, This rechristening will
be in consonance with the history, culture and identity of our State and will reflect the
”
aspirations of our people. After Independence, there have been many changes in the
names of many States and cities. The name ‘West Bengal’ came into existence when
the province of Bengal was partitioned in 1947. The eastern part came to be known as
‘East Pakistan’ and the western part was named as ‘West Bengal’. …(Interruptions)…
Today, there is no East Pakistan. After the Bangladesh Liberation War, it became
Bangladesh. …(Interruptions)…
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Please, सीट पर बठै कर न बोल(cid:514)।
